title: What A Museum Collection Looks Like When It Becomes Data
source: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API

charts.caption: Top departments in the 68,742-record Cleveland sample. Department counts show dataset shape, not cultural importance.
Creation-century buckets from normalized earliest creation dates; blunt time buckets hide date uncertainty.
Accession-number decade proxy; 7,739 mismatches against explicit accession_date in audit.
Visual availability in sample; 41,444 has image, 27,298 no image.

claimChecklist: Say this is a bounded 68,742-record sample, not the full Cleveland collection.
Mention 68,743 total API records were available at collection time.
Do not generalize from Cleveland to museums as a whole.
Treat accession decade as a proxy and disclose 7,739 accession-year mismatches.
Caption charts as sample charts, not complete collection charts.
Include audit caveats: 47,636 flagged rows, 27,298 no-image rows, and 37,779 rows with no provenance entries.
finalCopyNotes: Lead with the methodological observation: an open API changes the unit of attention from object to collection table.
Use the Cleveland sample as a first essay, not as a proxy for museum collections generally.
Keep acquisition-decade language tentative unless the audit rows are manually reviewed.
Use one to three charts in the post; the chart set is deliberately larger than the likely published figure set.
